name: routing-decomposer
description: Decompose, write, and grade the routing surface of a skill — its frontmatter description — on two crossing axes: INSTRUCTION (capability → scope → triggers → disambiguation → economy) and ROUTING (fires → holds → boundary → robustness → stability), scored separately so a description that reads well can't hide that it mis-routes. ROUTING uses a deterministic lexical-overlap eval over a labeled, adversarially-built corpus as a legibility AID — it lists the recall/precision holes by name (the truthful NOT-for fence repels sibling vocabulary); a human reads them, since a green F1 is not a pass and the proxy can't grade paraphrase (B4). INSTRUCTION gates on capability/scope honesty the eval can't see, pre-filtered by a static description linter. Backed by a gated rubric, a checked-in corpus + scorecard protocol, and before/after rewrites that move precision or recall. NOT for authoring or writing a whole skill end-to-end (skills-studio); NOT for grading a function on spec/execution (code-decomposer) or layouts/components/types/configs/queries (the in-repo *-decomposer siblings).
